verdict.rationale: Paddle documents API keys with granular permissions/scopes, rotation, and even recommends 'hard scoping via least-permission API keys' for MCP agent use, plus sandbox-only keys (pdl_sdbx_) for safe testing — giving a real path to scoped agent credentials. However, the MCP server itself 'doesn't gate destructive operations' and OAuth live connections only start with read access by default, so true least-privilege enforcement at the agent layer is partial and self-admitted as weak. missing for 10: no fine-grained per-agent scoping UI shown, no evidence of automated/expiring short-lived tokens for agents, and destructive-action gating is explicitly absent rather than enforced.
